basis: half the term energy's error, the 5P level being held exactly

basis: the same against 5P3/2
note: the nearer of the two on every rung above 5D

basis: half the term energy's error, as the row above

basis: the 5S half of the two-photon matrix element, normalised on the 6S rung

basis: rb5s6s.polarizability.alpha_5s at this rung's drive wavelength
note: the half of the differential polarizability this package holds for every rung

basis: half the 16 to 84 band of rb5s6s.polarizability.mc_band at 400 draws
note: the matrix elements, cores and tails drawn from their own quoted sigmas. Near a pole the band is asymmetric and the half-span understates the far side

basis: alpha(upper) minus alpha(5S), this package's own sum over states
note: the 993 nm sign is under dispute and the magnitude is what every bound reads

basis: half the 16 to 84 band of rb5s6s.polarizability.mc_band at 400 draws
note: ONLY the 5S side is drawn: mc_band samples the 5S and 6S ladders and this package states no sigmas for the 7S elements, so this is a LOWER BOUND on the true error and not the error

basis: at this rung's OWN achievable waist and the retro ratio of record
note: the waist is not common across rungs (A136), so this is not the polarizability ratio

basis: the polarizability, two powers of the waist and the retro ratio, in quadrature
note: the waist term dominates on every rung away from 993 nm, which is the finding this producer exists for

basis: both halves summed over the nP this package holds, on 6S
note: the element the ceiling divides by. The 5S-half row above ranks the intermediate resonance alone and reads higher on every rung whose upper element is the smaller half, the upper element being what that row holds common. This note carried the 7S numbers as literals until 2026-09-10 and was emitted on every rung, so the 6S row said 6.27 against 1.41 where both of its own cells read one

basis: drawn from the held reduced-element sigmas on both halves, twenty thousand draws, seeded
note: 1.69 per cent on the 7S rung. The elements are summed UNSIGNED here and the nP terms above 5P carry the opposite sign to the 5P ones, about four per cent of each element, which is a systematic this row does NOT carry

basis: the rung's own natural width over the 6S rung's, from the held lifetimes
note: enters all three ceiling rows below. Held common at one until 2026-09-10, which is what made the third of them an identity

basis: the two held lifetimes' own sigmas in quadrature, 45.57(17) and 88.07(40) ns
note: 0.59 per cent on the 7S rung. The ELEMENT ratio beside it carries 1.69 per cent from the held reduced-element sigmas, drawn rather than linearised, and the two together set the ceiling rows' own errors

basis: Delta-alpha times the natural width over the matrix element, against the 6S rung
note: the shift at which the two-photon Rabi frequency reaches a fixed fraction of the natural width. BELOW ONE MEANS THIS RUNG SATURATES EARLIER, which is the opposite of what a larger coefficient suggests on its own

basis: the width and element sigmas in quadrature, relative
note: the differential polarizability's own uncertainty is NOT in this row: carrying it is owed

basis: the square of the matrix element over the coefficient, divided by the natural width, against 6S
note: the shot-noise gain this rung offers at the SAME on-axis shift, which is where the ladder pays. The row below evaluates the same rate at each rung's own ceiling instead

basis: the width sigma and twice the element sigma, in quadrature
note: twice, because the rate carries the element squared. The differential polarizability's own uncertainty is owed here too

basis: the same rate evaluated at each rung's own saturation ceiling, which reduces to the natural width ratio
note: THIS ROW HAS BEEN READ THREE WAYS IN TWO DAYS and this is the first reading with the width in it. At the ceiling Omega = f Gamma, so the rate is f^2 Gamma and the ratio is the width ratio alone: every other factor cancels. It was published as one, first as the result and then as an algebraic identity, and both readings were artefacts of holding the width common. The ladder does NOT deliver the same signal at each rung's own saturation ceiling: a longer-lived upper state delivers less

basis: the width ratio's own sigma, since the row reduces to it
note: every other factor cancels exactly, so this row's error is the two lifetimes' and nothing else

basis: the nearest nP level of the held ladder, as a wavelength
note: what couples the upper state to the cell's own thermal field

basis: the term energy's error over the gap, the nP level being exact here
note: it is large where the gap is small, which is the high rungs

basis: 1/(exp(hv/kT) - 1) at 130 C, hv/kT = 5.44
note: above about a per cent the thermal field moves population out of the upper state at a fair fraction of its own decay rate

basis: the occupation's own derivative in the gap, times the gap's error
note: the cell temperature dominates this in practice and is not in this row: ten kelvin moves the occupation by about a fifth at the high rungs

basis: the cascade this rung emits on
note: the 993 nm rung is the only one the bench's installed 795 nm filter already serves. A cascade identification is not a measured value

basis: Rydberg-Ritz from the held anchors of this series
note: above the 5S1/2 ground state

basis: two-photon, 2e7 divided by the term energy in cm-1
note: inside the 650 to 1050 nm band this producer covers

basis: the two-fit spread on an extrapolated rung, a bound on the NIST precision on a held one
note: the held rows carry 0.01 cm-1, which is conservative for levels this low and is NOT a value this repository holds

basis: the two-fit spread and the Ritz form's own measured extrapolation error, in quadrature
